THE CONTRACT, NON-NEGOTIABLE:
- Write the smallest set of acceptance tests such that all of them passing
  means the ticket is done and nothing more is owed. Prefer one; three is
  a lot; more than five means the ticket needs splitting, not testing.
- Put them in a NEW test file of their own, beside the code, never
  appended to an existing test file. Its name MUST end in
  `.acceptance.test.<ext>` — `repo-settings.acceptance.test.ts`,
  `Plan.acceptance.test.tsx` — so a reader and the tooling can tell an
  acceptance test from a round's own at a glance. Later rounds write their own tests and run
  only those; the pod's Bash hook refuses the files listed under "Done
  when these pass" by name, so an acceptance test sharing a file with
  theirs would lock them out of their own test.
- RUN them — those, and nothing else. Not the repository's full suite,
  not lint, not the typechecker, not the formatter.
  CI is the judge of this branch and runs all of it on every push.
  Name the test files you run: the pod's Bash hook refuses a bare
  `npm test` or a `vitest run` with no path.
  Every acceptance test must fail, and fail for the RIGHT reason — the
  behaviour is absent, not the import path typo'd or a fixture missing.
- Quote the actual failure output in your final message. A test you did
  not run is not a red bar, it is a guess — unless this pod cannot run
  it at all, below.
- Do not weaken, skip or `.todo` a test to make the suite tidy. Red is the
  deliverable.

WHEN THIS POD CANNOT RUN THE TESTS. The pod carries Node and a few tools,
not every language's toolchain. If the command that runs your tests is
missing here — `java`, `mvn`, `gradle`, `go`, `cargo` or `dotnet` is not
found, or a wrapper such as `./mvnw` reports no `JAVA_HOME` — do not look
for it and do not install it: no `sudo`, no `apt`, no `find /`, no
download. The pull request's CI runs these tests on every push and proves
the red bar instead. Write the tests as the contract says, read each one
against the ticket's claim in place of running it, then commit and push.
In `.lore/dod.md`, right under the strategy, write that the red bar is
CI's to show and name the CI job that runs the tests. In your final
message, quote the command CI runs where the failure output would be.

real entry point — a function called, a component rendered, a binary
run. A test whose assertion subject is the repository's own source text

must not write one; it pins prose, not behaviour, and it outlives the
ticket as noise. The honest moves instead:
- "This prose drifts from a value" — make the prose compute the value

  fixture). Drift becomes impossible; no guard file exists.
- "This duplication must not come back" — the diff removing it and the
  existing tests staying green are the proof; a scan test is not.

  ticket owes no new test at all — that is what `mechanical` is for.

## When it fails

- **NIS-2 Article 21.** A `save` that rejects does not fail the turn: the caller still receives the answer, and the failure becomes exactly one logged line under category `orchestrator`, message `session save failed`, carrying the session id and the error's message ([validated by: keeps the turn alive and logs once when save rejects @bbdb399c](../../src/orchestration/sessionSave.test.ts#L48)).

- An `afterSession` hook that throws does not cost the turn its write signal: `save` still fires, and the hook's error still reaches the caller ([validated by: saves even when an afterSession hook throws @d4b4db54](../../src/orchestration/sessionSave.test.ts#L73)).
</document>
<document source="specs/hal-engine-tool-executor-throw/spec.md" type="spec" relevance="0.51" tokens="624">
## An executor that throws

- It is answered with a `result` naming the tool and saying the call failed, never the thrown message ([validated by: answers an executor that rejects with a result naming the tool, never the thrown message @de872866](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L175)).
- A throw of any shape is answered alike: a string, `undefined`, a plain object, and an object with no prototype, whose message cannot even be turned into a string ([validated by: answers a throw of any shape alike: a string, undefined, a plain object, an object with no prototype @20d8e40f](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L185)).
- The throw is logged once, at `error` under `tool` as `tool executor threw`, with the tool's name, the error's type and its message cut to 500 characters ([validated by: logs a throw once, at error under tool, with the tool name and error type, its message cut to 500 characters @77df51ff](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L195)).
- A throw after the call's `ToolContext.signal` was aborted for any reason but a timeout, as when its turn is abandoned because the socket closed, is no tool failure: it is logged at `info` instead, once, under `tool` as `tool call abandoned`, with the tool's name and the error's type, and writes no `error` line ([validated by: logs a throw after its signal was aborted, not timed out, at info as tool call abandoned, and no error line @c8b6c593](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L211)).
- A reason that is no error at all, such as a string or `null`, is no timeout either, so a throw after it is logged as abandoned too ([validated by: logs a throw as abandoned after a signal aborted with a reason that is no error, a string or null @ef69f1d5](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L225)).
- A throw while the signal is still live, or after it was aborted with a `TimeoutError`, the reason the orchestrator gives at a call's `toolTimeoutMs` deadline, is a failure, logged at `error` as `tool executor threw` ([validated by: keeps a throw at error as tool executor threw while its signal is live and after it timed out @ee9626ff](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L235)).
- The turn goes on to its answer and succeeds: `afterModelResponse` fires and `onError` does not ([validated by: answers a call whose executor threw, and the turn goes on to its answer with afterModelResponse and no onError @178206f1](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L770)).

# Definition of Done

> `beforeSession` is awaited before the `try` block opens, so a throw from it escapes before the `catch` and `finally` exist. Neither `onError` nor `afterSession` runs.

**Strategy: `direct`** — The orchestrator lifecycle hook seam already exists on `createChatOrchestrator`. Calling `processMessage` with a throwing `beforeSession` hook observes whether `onError` and `afterSession` fire before the error reaches the caller.

## Done when these pass

- [ ] **runs onError then afterSession when beforeSession throws, and still rejects to the caller** — When `beforeSession` throws, `onError` receives the error and session, `afterSession` receives the session, and the caller receives the original rejection.
  `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.acceptance.test.ts`

## Facets

- [ ] Move `beforeSession` invocation inside the `try` block in `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts`
- [ ] Keep existing tests in `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts` and `src/config.test.ts` green unedited
- [ ] Document in `CHANGELOG.md` that `onError` and `afterSession` now run when `beforeSession` throws

## Out of scope

- The `instanceof Error` gate on `onError` (owned by its own issue)
- Usage accounting across tool rounds (HALEngine#93)
